title: 2026 U.S. Senate election in South Carolina
description: South Carolina will elect one U.S. senator in 2026 for the state’s Class II seat, currently held by Republican Lindsey Graham. The race matters because it is one of the Senate contests that will help determine chamber control in 2026. South Carolina remains a strongly Republican state in federal elections, but Democrats are trying to make the race more competitive. The main contrast is between Graham’s long tenure, national-security profile, and close ties to the GOP establishment and challengers who are emphasizing cost of living, health care, accountability, and voter frustration with Washington.
polling_note: Public polling found in the last 90 days includes a Public Policy Polling survey of South Carolina voters conducted November 21-22, 2025, and reported by WCIV/ABC News 4.

candidates.name: Lindsey Graham
candidates.summary: Lindsey Graham is the incumbent U.S. senator from South Carolina and is seeking another term in 2026. His campaign presents him as a conservative focused on national security, lower federal spending, conservative judges, and support for Donald Trump.

Healthcare.stance: Advocates market-based reforms to reduce healthcare costs and premiums, and has opposed broad Obamacare subsidies. Has supported consumer-driven options such as Health Savings Accounts and backed reform plans aimed at replacing or scaling back Obamacare subsidies in favor of market-based approaches.

Economy.stance: Supports a targeted FY2026 budget resolution to fully fund ICE and Border Patrol for 3.5 years to secure the border; argues that disciplined, security-focused immigration spending is essential for economic stability and reducing illegal immigration costs.

Immigration.stance: Supports strict immigration enforcement and robust border security, including full funding for ICE and CBP. Has introduced the Updated End Sanctuary Cities Act of 2026 to end sanctuary city policies and restore federal enforcement authority.

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Lindsey Graham strongly defends Second Amendment rights, opposes broad new gun restrictions, and has urged strengthening enforcement of existing laws; he has supported actions to protect gun owners from federal overreach by pushing the ATF to strengthen Second Amendment protections and rescind Biden-era rules.

Climate/Energy.stance: Supports energy independence via expanded domestic energy production and resilient infrastructure, and backs targeted energy affordability and disaster-relief investments; has criticized broad federal clean-energy subsidies and advocates a conservative, targeted approach to energy and climate policy rather than sweeping reforms like the Green New Deal.

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Opposes broad federal protections for LGBTQ+ status in civil rights law; previously voted against the Respect for Marriage Act, supporting traditional marriage; stance updated to reflect that he opposed federal protections for same-sex marriage in 2022 and has historically expressed reservations about expanding LGBTQ+ rights beyond religious liberty protections.

Election Policy.stance: Supports election integrity measures, including requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register and photo ID to vote in federal elections; cosponsored the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE America Act), an expanded version of SAVE Act, to implement these requirements and to remove non-citizens from voter rolls.

Local Issues.stance: Supports targeted federal funding for South Carolina infrastructure and readiness, prioritizing local projects such as upgrades at Joint Base Charleston and Coast Guard Base Charleston and other SC infrastructure initiatives funded in FY2026 spending bills. flags.concern: Calvin Cowen is described as an 'active candidate who filed on March 27, 2026,' but no career history, education, website, or social media is provided. This is the most thinly documented candidate in the field. While acceptable under the missing-data policy (genuine scarcity of public information), human reviewer should confirm that Cowen is a bona fide active candidate and not a procedural registration without campaign infrastructure.

flags.concern: Calvin Cowen's Civil Rights stance mentions 'a federal law giving states authority over policies affecting transgender athletes' based on one news article. While the source is cited, this is Cowen's only documented policy position, and the phrasing (federal law giving states authority) is a specific policy mechanism that merits clarity on whether Cowen himself articulated this or if the news outlet inferred it.
flags.suggestion: Confirm whether Cowen's own statements endorse this specific framing or if the news outlet summarized his position; cite direct quotes if available.

flags.concern: Lindsey Graham's abortion stance cites NPR, Washington Post, and PBS NewsHour articles from 2022 and a 2022 Senate.gov press release—all well over three years old. While Graham's 15-week ban position has remained consistent, the citation dates are quite dated. Human reviewer should confirm whether Graham has issued any updated statements or clarifications since 2022.
flags.suggestion: Check for any 2024–2026 statements from Graham clarifying or revising his abortion position, or add a note that sources are from 2022 and reflect his most recent public stance.

reviews.summary: This is a well-constructed and comprehensively sourced profile of the 2026 South Carolina U.S. Senate race. The incumbent Lindsey Graham and five Democratic challengers (Annie Andrews, Kyle Freeman, Catherine Fleming Bruce, Brandon Brown) are documented with strong primary sourcing from official campaign sites, Senate press releases, and credible news outlets. Issue positions are consistently supported by cited URLs, and candidate backgrounds are verifiable against the sources provided. Language is predominantly neutral and nonpartisan across all candidates. The profile handles the candidate-limit constraint transparently and appropriately caps the field at 8 active candidates with a note explaining the selection rationale. Minor gaps in coverage for lesser-known Republican challengers (Calvin Cowen, Thomas Dismukes, Paul Dans) are acceptable given genuine absence of public information and are properly documented as 'low confidence' or 'no public position found.' Polling data is recent and clearly sourced. No internal contradictions or egregious bias detected.

flags.concern: The entry lists the same institution ('Massachusetts Institute of Technology') twice for the same degree type.
The field is null for a candidate who is a professional in logistics. While not a factual error, adding a date range would improve the profile's completeness if such information becomes available.

The stance references a specific Facebook post as the sole source. While this source is cited, it represents a specific reaction rather than a comprehensive policy platform. This is acceptable given the lack of broader policy materials.

reviews.summary: This candidate profile is excellent, demonstrating high-quality research and rigorous adherence to the provided sources. The profile successfully balances the presentation of a complex, multi-candidate primary field with a neutral, non-partisan tone. Candidate backgrounds are well-integrated with cited evidence, and the documentation of 'no public position found' for certain issues is appropriate and helpful, indicating thorough research efforts rather than gaps in data.

flags.suggestion: Add a brief note that sample size was not disclosed in the cited Facebook post.

reviews.summary: Strong, well-sourced profile with consistent internal sourcing across all major candidates. Lindsey Graham’s issue positions are backed by official Senate and campaign URLs; Annie Andrews and other Democratic candidates have direct campaign-site citations. Minor candidates (Cowen, Dismukes, etc.) appropriately show “no public position found” after documented searches rather than fabricated stances. Language is neutral and avoids partisan framing. Background details for Graham, Andrews, Dans, and others align with the cited Ballotpedia, campaign, and official sources.
